clue.text: Immediate payment required to glimpse 1984 Wimbledon champion

parts.note: to glimpse something is to spot it
Pat Cash, the Australian tennis player, won the Wimbledon men's singles title (in 1987, in fact)

explanation.surface: A demand for instant payment before one may catch sight of a tennis star.
explanation.walkthrough: Pat Cash actually won Wimbledon in 1987, so the year in the clue appears to be the setter's slip; the name is what matters.
explanation.definitionFit: Spot cash is money paid on the spot, at the moment of sale, so it is payment made without delay.

clue.text: Extravagant display is an odds-on hit

parts.note: SP is the racing abbreviation for starting price, the odds offered on a horse
to lash is to strike or hit hard

explanation.surface: A betting tip: a lavish show is a heavy favourite to be a success.
explanation.definitionFit: A splash is a showy, conspicuous display, as in making a splash with money.

clue.text: Compensation for not filming

parts.note: off is the opposite of on, so it stands for not
an actor who is filming is on set, so not filming means being off set

explanation.surface: Payment owed to an actor for the days spent not shooting scenes.
explanation.definitionFit: An offset is something that balances or counteracts a loss, a form of making amends.

clue.text: 1,and each identical

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as '1,and each identical' (5) for CLONE: the opening '1' looks like an OCR misread or a cut, and no parse or search recovers the printed clue.

clue.text: Body-builder becomes so tired

indicators.note: becomes signals that the letters of the following words turn into something else by rearrangement

explanation.surface: A weightlifter running out of energy after a long workout.
explanation.definitionFit: Anabolic steroids are drugs used to build muscle mass, so one is literally a builder of the body.

clue.text: Swear to having visited Lord's

parts.note: someone who has visited a place has been at it
Lord's is the London cricket ground that hosts Test matches, international cricket games

explanation.surface: A cricket fan vowing they really did go to the famous ground.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord's is a London cricket ground; to have visited it for a match is to have been at a Test.
explanation.definitionFit: To attest is to bear witness or declare something true under oath.

clue.text: Where undergraduates direct their studies? Rather!

definitions.meaning: students study towards a qualification, a university award
rather here means somewhat or to some extent

explanation.definitionFit: Students work towards a university qualification, and the phrase also means somewhat or quite, the sense of rather.

clue.text: Bill enters jailbreak just for a prank

indicators.note: enters says one piece goes inside the other, here the bill entering the jailbreak

parts.note: a jailbreak is an escape from prison
AD is short for advertisement, a bill posted up

explanation.surface: A prisoner breaks out merely as a practical joke.
explanation.definitionFit: An escapade is a reckless or mischievous adventure, a bit of fun-making like a prank.

clue.text: Indefatigable, but can't get the wheels in motion

definitions.text: can't get the wheels in motion
definitions.meaning: a vehicle without tyres (American spelling tires) cannot roll

explanation.surface: A determined motorist who is nonetheless stuck because the car won't move.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the word as tire-less: lacking tyres, using the American spelling, so the wheels cannot turn.
explanation.definitionFit: Indefatigable means never growing weary, which is the plain sense of untiring.

clue.text: Spare the thought that Communism is dead

definitions.meaning: spare here means surplus, remaining unused

definitions.text: the thought that Communism is dead
definitions.meaning: the political left being finished or over

explanation.definitionFit: Spare food is what remains after a meal, and the second reading says the political left is finished.

clue.text: Relish recipe for making a dish

parts.note: a relish is a sauce or condiment
R is the abbreviation for recipe, from the Latin on prescriptions

explanation.surface: Instructions for preparing a condiment to fill a bowl.
explanation.definitionFit: A saucer is a small shallow dish set under a cup.

clue.text: Cry very little and softly

parts.note: wee is Scottish for small or tiny
P stands for piano, the musical direction to play softly

explanation.surface: Someone sobbing quietly, just a tiny bit.
explanation.definitionFit: To weep is to shed tears, a synonym of to cry.

clue.text: Deserve to be replaced as a docker

indicators.note: be replaced tells the solver to put the letters of the preceding words in fresh positions

explanation.surface: A dock worker who has earned being sacked and swapped for someone else.
explanation.definitionFit: A stevedore is a person who loads and unloads ships, the work of a dockworker.

clue.text: Fish is about ten pence for cashier

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the fish is placed around the other pieces

parts.note: an eel is a fish
X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: A fishmonger pricing a fish at around ten pence for the person on the till.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cashier' looks like the bank clerk, but here it is the verb meaning to dismiss from service, especially the armed forces.
explanation.definitionFit: To cashier is to dismiss someone dishonourably from the forces, which is to throw them out.

clue.text: One embraced by infatuated girl

indicators.note: embraced by says the first piece is held inside the second

parts.note: to be mad about someone is to be infatuated
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone hugged by a lovestruck young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Maid is an old word for a young unmarried woman.

clue.text: Take steps to carry a cake-lots of it

parts.note: a bun is a small cake
to dance is to take steps in rhythm

explanation.surface: A dance where the participants must carry a cake, and plenty of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Abundance is a great plenty, a large quantity of something.

clue.text: Marches airborne troops around Delaware

indicators.note: around signals that the troops surround the state

parts.note: paras are paratroopers, soldiers dropped by parachute
DE is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Delaware

explanation.surface: Paratroopers on manoeuvres in an American state.
explanation.definitionFit: Parades are ceremonial processions, marching in formation.

clue.text: Bridge champion gets given a beating

parts.note: a span is a bridge or the arch of one
a king is a champion, the best in a field

explanation.surface: The winner of a bridge tournament is thrashed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bridge' suggests the card game, but it is the structure, a span.
explanation.definitionFit: A spanking is a beating given with the open hand.

clue.text: Appreciative of speed during Gulf conflict

indicators.note: during means within, so speed is placed inside the other piece
conflict suggests the letters of the word next to it are in turmoil and get rearranged

parts.note: rate means speed, as in rate of knots

explanation.surface: A remark about how quickly something happened in the Gulf War.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conflict' rearranges GULF to GFUL, and 'during' puts RATE inside it after the G.
explanation.definitionFit: To be grateful is to feel thanks, to appreciate what was done.

clue.text: False testimony by a panel of judges

parts.note: per means by, as in per post
a jury is a body of people who judge a case

explanation.surface: Lying to a court in front of the jury.
explanation.definitionFit: Perjury is lying under oath, giving untrue evidence in court.

clue.text: You'll say it's the festive season

indicators.note: say tells the solver that the word is to be spoken, giving a word that matches it in pronunciation

parts.note: the contraction of you will

explanation.surface: A cheery prediction that Christmas will be spoken of.
explanation.definitionFit: Yule is an old name for the Christmas period.

clue.text: Article about yours truly is the last word

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the article goes round the other piece

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
yours truly is a jocular way of saying me

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece about the writer has the final say.
explanation.definitionFit: Amen is said at the end of a prayer, literally the closing word.

clue.text: Antagonistic to poetry of Christian times

parts.note: AD, Anno Domini, marks the years of the Christian era
verse is poetry

explanation.surface: Someone hostile to religious poems of the early church.
explanation.definitionFit: Adverse means hostile or opposing, contrary to someone's interests.

clue.text: Declare that a lock needs to be raised

indicators.note: in a down clue being raised means read from bottom to top, so the word is turned around

parts.note: a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: A statement that a lock must be lifted to open it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To be raised' in this down clue turns TRESS upwards to give SSERT.
explanation.definitionFit: To assert is to state firmly, to declare something to be so.

clue.text: How an earl is beaten?

parts.note: a '... earl' is a traditional phrase for a nobleman wearing the belt of his rank, and the word also means thrashed

explanation.surface: Asking how a nobleman gets thrashed.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'belted earl' is a stock phrase for an earl, from the belt worn at his investiture; the word also means hit hard.
explanation.definitionFit: Being hit with a strap is one sense of the word, and the belted earl is a stock phrase for a peer.

clue.text: Recorded the Poet Laureate's absence

parts.note: absence means there is none, which is no
Ted Hughes was Britain's Poet Laureate from 1984 to 1998

explanation.surface: A note that the national poet failed to attend.
explanation.walkthrough: The Poet Laureate's absence reads as 'no Ted': Ted Hughes held the post when the puzzle appeared.
explanation.definitionFit: Something noted has been written down, put on record.

clue.text: Matter of current concern to child survivors

definitions.meaning: a topical question still under debate
issue means offspring, so living issue are children still alive

explanation.definitionFit: A topical matter is one still being debated, and in law issue means offspring, so living children.

clue.text: One minute before time or something very close

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Being one minute early or arriving just in time.
explanation.definitionFit: A spitting likeness is a near copy, so a close resemblance is a likeness of the person.

clue.text: Spanish princess without a baby

indicators.note: without means lacking, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: an infanta is a daughter of a Spanish or Portuguese monarch

explanation.surface: A Spanish royal who has no child.
explanation.definitionFit: An infant is a very young child.

clue.text: Embellish ten Roman pieces

indicators.note: pieces suggests the words are broken up and reassembled in another order

explanation.surface: Decorating with ten fragments of Roman artefacts.
explanation.definitionFit: To ornament is to decorate or adorn.

clue.text: A man of course to hit back with little hesitation

indicators.note: back tells the solver to read the word backwards

parts.note: to flog is to hit or beat
er is a short sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Someone who naturally strikes back after barely a pause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A man of course' sounds like 'naturally', but the course is a golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: A player on a golf links is a person who frequents a course.

clue.text: Abhorred action taken about examination

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the action goes round the examination

parts.note: a deed is an act or action
a test is an examination

explanation.surface: Someone hated the steps taken over an exam.
explanation.definitionFit: Detested means hated intensely, the same as abhorred.
